beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sai Pranavi J. This video is about a dashboard whose severity counts went blind the moment its fixture data got old enough, a seven-day filter that quietly zeroed out Critical and High, forever, while the list right below it kept showing the real thing.
beats.new_visual_element: Personal-intro card: name + one-line plain-language summary, spoken

shot.note: Same pattern as this fellow's other episodes' B01.

beats.narration_text: The data this dashboard reads from was loaded back in July. Today is November nineteenth, four months later. And the severity query behind the stats cards only ever looked back seven days. Seven days, against data four months stale, is zero, every single time.
beats.new_visual_element: Fixture date range (July 14 to July 24, 2026) next to today's date (November 19, 2026) and the seven-day window, with the arithmetic flagged as impossible

shot.note: Real dates from the live DB and F1-VERIFICATION.md, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Here's the real query. It counted Critical, High, Medium, and Low, but only from rows created in the last seven days. Total Feeds, right next to it on the same dashboard, had no such filter. And the feed list underneath, the one with Select All, loads the hundred most recent items, no date filter either. So the cards said Critical: zero, High Priority: zero. The list below them was full of both.
beats.new_visual_element: The real pre-fix WHERE created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days' clause, the real Stats.jsx labels (Total Feeds, Critical, High Priority), and the real unwindowed list_feeds ordering with the frontend's real limit: 100, shown verbatim

shot.note: [Source: Regulatory_QA/backend/app/crud.py (pre-fix), Stats.jsx, App.jsx; F1-VERIFICATION.md] Verbatim pre-fix query and labels, not paraphrased.

beats.narration_text: The fix is one line: drop the seven-day filter from the severity query, so it reads the same unwindowed population as Total Feeds and the feed list already do. Source breakdown's thirty-day window, and recent activity's fourteen-day window, stay untouched. Recent activity is supposed to be a time series, and source breakdown isn't contradicted by an always-visible panel the way severity was.
beats.new_visual_element: The real one-line diff removing the WHERE clause, plus a note on what was deliberately left alone

shot.note: [Source: F1-VERIFICATION.md, 'The fix'] Real diff, matches the committed fix exactly.

beats.narration_text: I ran both versions of the query directly against the live database. The old query, with the seven-day window: zero, zero, zero, zero. The new query, unwindowed: thirty-three Critical, ninety-eight High, two hundred eighty Medium, matching last week's independently verified counts exactly. And the feed list's actual top hundred items, same database, no date filter: twenty-four Critical, eight High, right there to click.
beats.new_visual_element: The real before/after table from this session's own live Postgres run: 0/0/0/0 versus 33/98/280/0, plus the 24/8 top-100 slice

shot.note: [Source: verification/verify_stale_stats_window_output.txt; F1-VERIFICATION.md] Real measured results from this session's own live-DB run, matching F1-VERIFICATION.md's own table exactly.

beats.narration_text: Two honest limits. First: source breakdown still has its own thirty-day window, with the same staleness risk as the one just fixed, not touched this round. A reasonable follow-up, not required to close this bug. Second: this was verified by running the real query text straight against the live database, not by loading the dashboard in a running browser session. No frontend or backend server was up this session.
beats.new_visual_element: 2 honest-limit cards, side by side, full weight: source_distribution's own unaddressed 30-day window, and no live browser/frontend session

shot.note: [Source: F1-VERIFICATION.md 'What's NOT touched'; RUN_LOG.md 2026-11-19 'Open issues'] Full weight, not softened.

beats.narration_text: A dashboard's summary is only as honest as the window it looks through. And a window that quietly stops matching the data underneath it is worse than no window at all.
